exact.Вот трамвайный билет. Трамваев в Любляне: Here's a tram ticket. There haven't been trams in Ljubljana for ages, but I've still got the ticket, it sits in a book as a bookmark, and I never seem to finish that book.

exact.продавщица в торговом центре в Савско на: a shop assistant at the shopping centre in Savsko naselje
exact.Меня взяли продавщицей в новый торговый: They took me on as a shop assistant at the new shopping centre in Savsko naselje. The blocks around it were new and tall, and the customers were as new as the blocks, nobody knew anybody yet.

exact.учительница деревенской школы: a teacher at a village school

exact.На пенсию я ушла из школы. Бывшие ученик: I retired from the school. Former pupils send me cards for the holidays, with mistakes in them, and of course I don't show them to anyone.
exact.торговка на городском рынке: a seller at the town market

exact.На рынок я перестала ездить, когда стало: I stopped going to market when the baskets got too heavy to carry. I still buy vegetables in the shop, only after giving them a good telling-off.

exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в Любляну: When I was very small, the Spanish flu came to Ljubljana. I don't remember it, but Mum said later that the hospital was overflowing then and lots of people were nursed at home.
exact.Летом восемнадцатого в Любляну пришла ис: In the summer of eighteen the Spanish flu came to Ljubljana, and in the autumn lots of schools were closed. At first we were glad we didn't have to study, until we understood why.

exact.Это совпало с концом войны и со всеми пе: It came at the same time as the end of the war and all the changes of that autumn, and in the stories at home it all ran together. They talked more about how every morning they counted who in the house was still coughing.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в Любляне: When I was very small, a new state was proclaimed on Congress Square in Ljubljana. I was told about it later, always with details of who stood where.

exact.Словенский стал единственным языком в шк: Slovene became the only language at school, and they gave us new textbooks.
exact.Одни радовались вслух, другие ждали, чем: Some were glad out loud, others waited to see how it would all end, and that could happen in one and the same family. In ours too, I think.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в Любляну: When I was very small, Italian troops entered Ljubljana. I don't remember it, and the grown-ups said little about it.
exact.Одиннадцатого апреля в Любляну вошли ита: On the eleventh of April Italian troops entered Ljubljana, and then a curfew came in and we were told to hand in our wireless sets. In the evenings it got so quiet you could hear the clock ticking.

On the eleventh of April Italian troops entered Ljubljana, and the mayor handed them the keys to the city by the church in Vič. In May Italy declared us its province, a curfew came in, we were told to hand in our wireless sets, and cycling was banned.

exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в Любляне: When I was very small, people in Ljubljana were taken away and hostages were shot. I was told about it much later, when I was old enough to understand.

exact.С сентября сорок первого итальянские вла: From September forty-one the Italian authorities sent the people they thought suspicious into internment, and from November a military court was at work and hostages began to be shot. People learnt of it from one another and spoke very quietly.
exact.Мы привыкли не задерживаться на улице и: We got used to not lingering in the street and not asking unnecessary questions.

exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, Любляну о: When I was very small, Ljubljana was fenced in with barbed wire, and you couldn't leave the city without a pass. I know that from the grown-ups.
exact.В феврале сорок второго вокруг Любляны з: In February forty-two they closed a ring of barbed wire round Ljubljana in a single day. To get past it you needed a pass, and beyond the wire were relatives, and vegetable plots, and milk.
exact.Двадцать третьего февраля вокруг Любляны: On the twenty-third of February they closed a ring of barbed wire round Ljubljana, thirty-odd kilometres of it. By evening you could only leave the city with a pass, and what used to come in from the villages arrived only now and then.
exact.Так, за проволокой, город и прожил до ма: And so, behind the wire, the city lived until May forty-five.
exact.Каждую поездку к родне за город теперь н: Every trip to relatives outside town now began with the question of whether they'd give you a pass.
exact.Город стал как большой двор с забором, в: The city became like a big yard with a fence, everyone in plain view of everyone else. Now there's a path along that line, people walk there, and to me it's strange and, I suppose, right.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, итальянцы ушли,: When I was small, the Italians left and the Germans took their place at the wire. I know that from the grown-ups.
exact.Осенью сорок третьего Италия капитулиров: In the autumn of forty-three Italy capitulated, and German soldiers stood at the posts by the wire instead of Italian ones. We children thought at first that now they'd take the wire down, but they didn't.
exact.После капитуляции Италии в сентябре соро: After Italy capitulated in September forty-three, German soldiers took over the posts, barracks and bunkers along the wire round Ljubljana. The city stayed the centre of the same province, only now the rule was German.
exact.Проволока осталась на месте, сменились т: The wire stayed where it was, only the people guarding it changed.
exact.Пришлось привыкать к другим приказам и к: We had to get used to different orders and a different language at the posts.
exact.Многие сначала надеялись, что станет лег: Lots of people hoped at first it would get easier, and soon stopped hoping. And in forty-five they started sending young people to dig trenches round the city, and that's what we talked about most at home.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в мае в Л: When I was very small, in May the Yugoslav Army entered Ljubljana, and the war was over for the city. I know that from the grown-ups.

exact.После нескольких дней боёв немецкие част: After several days of fighting the German units and the Home Guard left Ljubljana for Carinthia, and on the morning of the ninth of May the Yugoslav Army entered the city. exact.Девятое мая так и осталось у нас праздни: The ninth of May has stayed our city's holiday ever since.

exact.Вечером теперь договаривались не о том,: In the evenings people now arranged not where to go but whose place to gather at.

exact.В девяностом в Словении прошли выборы, г: In ninety there were elections in Slovenia with lots of parties, and then a plebiscite on independence. I know that from what people told me.
exact.В девяностом прошли выборы, где было из: In ninety there were elections where you actually had a choice, and in December a plebiscite on independence.
exact.Весной девяностого прошли первые после в: In the spring of ninety there were the first elections since the war with lots of parties, and on the twenty-third of December there was the plebiscite on independence. Nearly everyone came, and nearly everyone said "yes".
exact.В очереди в магазине теперь спорили не о: In the shop queue people now argued not about prices but about parties, and sometimes about prices too.
exact.На плебисцит я пошла с утра, чтобы не ст: I went to the plebiscite first thing in the morning so as not to queue, and there was already a queue. It was unfamiliar and a little frightening, as if you were signing a paper you hadn't read to the end.
exact.В девяносто первом Словения провозгласил: In ninety-one Slovenia declared independence. I know that from what people told me.
exact.В конце июня девяносто первого Словения: At the end of June ninety-one Slovenia declared independence, and a new flag was raised on Republic Square.
exact.Двадцать пятого июня Скупщина приняла ак: On the twenty-fifth of June the Assembly passed the independence acts, and on the evening of the twenty-sixth a new flag was raised on Republic Square. Planes flew low over the square, everyone tipped their heads back, and nobody knew what it meant.
exact.Слово «республика» вдруг стало значить с: The word "republic" suddenly meant something quite different from before.
exact.Молодые радовались громко, а я больше сл: The young ones were glad out loud, and I mostly listened. Joy and worry came together, and I didn't know which of them to show the neighbours.
exact.В девяносто первом в Словении была корот: In ninety-one there was a short war in Slovenia, ten days. I know that from what people told me.

exact.В девяносто первом в Словении появились: In ninety-one Slovenia got its own money, the tolar. I know that from what people told me.

exact.Восьмого октября кончился трёхмесячный м: On the eighth of October the three-month moratorium ran out, and we got our own money, the tolar. For three days dinars were exchanged for temporary vouchers, one for one, and our own customs started work at the borders.
exact.Цены я ещё долго пересчитывала в уме на: For a long time I still converted prices into dinars in my head, though there was no sense in it at all.
exact.Боны были бумажные, совсем простые, и не: The vouchers were paper, quite plain, and it was hard to believe they were real money. I looked at my first ones like a train ticket to who knows where.

exact.Первого января седьмого года толар смени: On the first of January two thousand and seven the euro replaced the tolar, and in December checks at the borders with our EU neighbours were abolished. It wasn't the first time I'd changed money, and nothing surprised me any more.

exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как зоопарк пере: I was told later how the zoo moved to Rožnik.
